correctness.rationale: For positive (a,b,c,d,e) and word 0^a1^b0^c1^d0^e, reconstructed exhaustive classification by number of transitions in a square root. A nonunary root has either one transition, giving only (0^c1^b)^2 if c<=a,b<=d or (1^d0^c)^2 if c<=e,d<=b, or two transitions, giving (0^i1^b0^(c-i))^2 when b=d and max(1,c-e)<=i<=min(a,c-1). Unary squares add floor(P/2)+floor(Q/2), P=max(a,c,e), Q=max(b,d); these root categories are distinct. Thus S=floor(P/2)+floor(Q/2)+alpha+beta+H and all mixed squares have the one length 2(c+min(b,d)). The case inequalities bound S<=floor(n/2), mixed T<=floor((n+1)/3), with witnesses for every n>=5. Counting b,i,k and nonnegative outer extensions gives H expectation GF z^6/((1-z)^2(1-z^2)^3); counting H>0 gives z^6(1+z+z^2)/((1-z)^4(1+z)^3). Dominant poles yield E[H]->1/8 and P(H>0)~3/(2n); normalized uniform five-compositions converge to Dirichlet(1,1,1,1,1), with limiting square density half of max of zero-run proportions plus max of one-run proportions, mean 1/3. Independent direct substring-set enumeration for all 5^5=3125 positive tuples in [1,5]^5 matched the complete list, counts and upper bounds. Finite testing corroborates the all-length transition/counted-composition arguments.
